orchestrated.text: A single agent auditing three independent code modules runs serially in 10.6 seconds and piles 52.4 thousand tokens into one window, far past the thirty-two thousand token cliff. Multi-agent orchestration fans the modules out to isolated specialists, cutting wall time to 6.4 seconds while keeping the coordinator compact.

The architecture separates three planes. On top sits the orchestrator hub with its own root context stack. Below it sit three specialist module blades, each with an isolated context tray. On the base plane sit external tool valves, an independent verifier gate, and the shared artifact vault.
The orchestrator spends 0.9 seconds decomposing the audit into three independent module tasks, then dispatches compact specifications down all three conduits at once.

All three module workers think, call their tool valves, and distill summaries concurrently. Because the branches overlap, the work phase finishes in 3.4 seconds instead of 8.6 seconds, bounded by the slowest branch on View A.

Each worker absorbs its own raw tool output locally, peaking at 18.0 thousand tokens. Each distills a compact summary, 5.6 thousand tokens in all, keeping the orchestrator at 8.6 thousand tokens at fan-in instead of 50.0 thousand, trading higher aggregate token spend for clean windows.

When the Search tool valve times out on the third worker, only that lane retries. Because 1.2 seconds of the 1.7 second retry overlap the Billing branch, wall time grows by just 0.9 seconds and the orchestrator's context stays untouched.

Before synthesis, an independent verifier gate inspects the merged summaries in a clean 6.4 thousand token window for 1.0 seconds to catch cross-module conflicts, sending critique back on failure or committing to the artifact vault before the orchestrator synthesizes in 1.1 seconds.

monolith.text: A single monolithic agent audits all three independent modules one after another in 10.6 seconds. Worse, every raw tool output piles into one shared context window, swelling to 52.4 thousand tokens and breaking past the thirty-two thousand token attention cliff.

In the single-agent baseline, one active agent plans on top with one shared context stack. Only the center compute lane executes tasks, calling the three external tool valves one by one before writing to the artifact vault, with no isolated worker trays and no separate verifier.
The single agent spends 0.9 seconds and 3.0 thousand tokens outlining the audit, then starts the Auth module alone while the Billing and Search modules wait in queue.
Each module runs its full think, tool call, and distill turn serially through the single active lane and tool valves. The three work branches add up to 8.6 seconds, stretching View A across the axis.

Without context isolation, all 47.0 thousand tokens of raw module logs stack directly onto the single shared window, hitting 50.0 thousand tokens before final synthesis and breaking past the red thirty-two thousand token collar.
When the Search tool valve times out, a 1.7 second retry adds the full delay straight onto the serial run, pushing total time to 12.3 seconds and adding error trace noise to the shared window.
With no independent verifier, the single agent self-checks and synthesizes its answer in 1.1 seconds inside the same 52.4 thousand token window before committing to the artifact vault.
